title: Integration by Parts
lead: Integration by parts, a technique built on the product rule, exchanges one integral for another, possibly easier, one. Here the reader learns to choose its two parts with LIATE, to apply it more than once, and to use it on definite integrals for an area and a volume.
objectives: Recognize when to use integration by parts.
Use the integration-by-parts formula to solve integration problems.
Use the integration-by-parts formula for definite integrals.
summary_html:
• The integration-by-parts formula allows the exchange of one integral for another, possibly easier, integral.
  • Integration by parts applies to both definite and indefinite integrals.

Derive the following formulas using the technique of integration by parts. Assume that n is a positive integer. These formulas are called reduction formulas because the exponent in the x term has been reduced by one in each case. The second integral is simpler than the original integral.

$\int x^{n}e^{x}dx=x^{n}e^{x}-n\int x^{n-1}e^{x}dx$

answer.solution: Choose $u=x^{n}$ and $dv=e^{x}dx,$ so that $du=nx^{n-1}dx$ and $v=e^{x}.$ Equation 7.1 then gives $\int x^{n}e^{x}dx=x^{n}e^{x}-\int e^{x}\cdot nx^{n-1}dx=x^{n}e^{x}-n\int x^{n-1}e^{x}dx,$ the formula, with the power of $x$ lowered by one.

exercises.prompt:
Derive the following formulas using the technique of integration by parts. Assume that n is a positive integer. These formulas are called reduction formulas because the exponent in the x term has been reduced by one in each case. The second integral is simpler than the original integral.

$\int x^{n}\cos x\;dx =x^{n}\sin x-n\int x^{n-1}\sin x\;dx$

answer.solution: Choose $u=x^{n}$ and $dv=\cos x\;dx,$ so that $du=nx^{n-1}dx$ and $v=\sin x.$ Equation 7.1 then gives $\int x^{n}\cos x\;dx=x^{n}\sin x-\int \sin x\cdot nx^{n-1}dx=x^{n}\sin x-n\int x^{n-1}\sin x\;dx.$

exercises.prompt:
Derive the following formulas using the technique of integration by parts. Assume that n is a positive integer. These formulas are called reduction formulas because the exponent in the x term has been reduced by one in each case. The second integral is simpler than the original integral.

$\int x^{n}\sin x\;dx =\underset{\_\_\_\_\_\_}{}$

answer.solution: Choose $u=x^{n}$ and $dv=\sin x\;dx,$ so that $du=nx^{n-1}dx$ and $v=-\cos x.$ Equation 7.1 then gives $\int x^{n}\sin x\;dx=-x^{n}\cos x+n\int x^{n-1}\cos x\;dx.$

exercises.prompt:
Integrate $\int 2x\sqrt{2x-3} dx$ using two methods:

a. Using parts, letting $dv=\sqrt{2x-3}\;dx$

b. Substitution, letting $u=2x-3$

State whether you would use integration by parts to evaluate the integral. If so, identify u and dv. If not, describe the technique used to perform the integration without actually doing the problem.

$\int x\;\ln x\;dx$

answer.solution: Use integration by parts. The integrand holds a logarithmic and an algebraic function, and L comes before A in LIATE, so $u=\ln x$ and $dv=x\;dx;$ then $du=\frac{1}{x}dx$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}x^{2},$ and the new integral $\int \frac{1}{2}x\;dx$ is easy.

exercises.prompt:
State whether you would use integration by parts to evaluate the integral. If so, identify u and dv. If not, describe the technique used to perform the integration without actually doing the problem.

$\int \frac{{\ln }^{2}x}{x}dx$

answer.solution: Do not use integration by parts. Choose u to be $\ln x,$ and the integral is of the form $\int u^{2}du .$

exercises.prompt:
State whether you would use integration by parts to evaluate the integral. If so, identify u and dv. If not, describe the technique used to perform the integration without actually doing the problem.

$\int xe^{x}dx$

answer.solution: Use integration by parts. A comes before E in LIATE, so $u=x$ and $dv=e^{x}dx;$ then $du=dx$ and $v=e^{x},$ and the new integral $\int e^{x}dx$ is easy.

exercises.prompt:
State whether you would use integration by parts to evaluate the integral. If so, identify u and dv. If not, describe the technique used to perform the integration without actually doing the problem.

$\int xe^{x^{2}-3}dx$

answer.solution: Do not use integration by parts. Let $u=x^{2}-3,$ and the integral can be put into the form $\int e^{u}du .$

exercises.prompt:
State whether you would use integration by parts to evaluate the integral. If so, identify u and dv. If not, describe the technique used to perform the integration without actually doing the problem.

$\int x^{2}\sin x\;dx$

answer.solution: Use integration by parts, twice. A comes before T in LIATE, so $u=x^{2}$ and $dv=\sin x\;dx;$ then $du=2x\;dx$ and $v=-\cos x,$ and the new integral $\int 2x\cos x\;dx$ needs integration by parts again, with $u=2x$ and $dv=\cos x\;dx.$

exercises.prompt:
State whether you would use integration by parts to evaluate the integral. If so, identify u and dv. If not, describe the technique used to perform the integration without actually doing the problem.

$\int x^{2}\sin (3x^{3}+2)dx$

answer.solution: Do not use integration by parts. Choose u to be $u=3x^{3}+2$ and the integral can be put into the form $\int \sin (u)du .$

For the following exercises, determine whether the statement is true or false. Justify your answer with a proof or a counterexample.

$\int e^{x}\sin (x)dx$ cannot be integrated by parts.

answer.solution: False. Integration by parts works on it, applied twice: with $u=\sin x$ and $dv=e^{x}dx,$ and then $u=\cos x$ and $dv=e^{x}dx,$ the original integral reappears on the right, and solving for it, as in Example 7.5, gives $\int e^{x}\sin x\;dx=\frac{1}{2}e^{x}(\sin x-\cos x)+C.$
